question: What underlying condition is the most frequent cause of oesophageal varices (enlarged veins)?

options.A: Portal hypertension from liver cirrhosis
options.B: Chronic bacterial infection of the stomach
options.C: Enlargement of the thyroid gland in the neck
options.D: Severe long-term dietary iron deficiency

explanation: When the liver is scarred (cirrhosis), blood can't flow through it easily. This backs up pressure into nearby vessels, including the fragile veins in the oesophagus.

question: Where should the money come from to pay for drugs given out under an exemption policy?

options.A: Extra fees charged secretly to other ordinary patients
options.B: Deductions taken directly from the personal salaries of nurses
options.C: Dedicated external subsidy pools, grants, or hospital subventions
options.D: Donations collected from patients waiting in the outpatient queue

explanation: External funds or hospital subventions must reimburse the DRF account so that providing free care to the poor doesn't ruin the pharmacy stock.

question: When taking a drug history from a patient in a Nigerian hospital, what must you make sure to ask about?

options.A: Focusing solely on medications taken in the last 24 hours
options.B: Asking only about expensive brand-name medications
options.C: Including traditional herbs and over-the-counter remedies
options.D: Recording only the drugs prescribed by the current hospital

explanation: Many patients take local herbs and chemist drugs alongside hospital meds. Asking about them helps prevent dangerous drug clashes!

question: Why is proper waste management in a health facility considered a crucial part of infection control?

options.A: It prevents environmental reservoirs from harboring and spreading pathogens
options.B: It lowers the overall financial cost of purchasing medications
options.C: It guarantees that patients will never develop drug allergies
options.D: It completely eliminates the need for nurses to wash their hands

explanation: Safe disposal of contaminated waste removes potential reservoirs where infectious agents can multiply and reach new hosts. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T95#GNS214_U1_T95_h7)

question: What is the main way functional nursing is organized?

options.A: Allowing patients to manage their own treatments without staff help
options.B: Giving one registered nurse total 24-hour responsibility for a single patient
options.C: Assigning specific tasks like medication administration to different staff members
options.D: Having a team leader direct nurse aides to bathe patients

explanation: Functional nursing divides the work by jobs: one person does all dressings, another gives all meds. It's like a production line!

question: What is a great food tip for a patient who feels nauseated and has a poor appetite during cancer treatment?

options.A: Eat three large heavy meals at traditional times
options.B: Offer small, frequent meals that are high in protein
options.C: Avoid all protein and eat only plain white sugar
options.D: Eat food straight from the oven while it is piping hot and aromatic

explanation: Large meals can overwhelm a weak tummy. Small, protein-rich snacks are much easier to handle and help keep their strength up!

question: What is usually the very first physical sign of puberty in young females?

options.A: Breast development
options.B: Growth of pubic hair
options.C: First menstrual period
options.D: Widening of the hips

explanation: Breast budding, known medically as thelarche, is typically the earliest visible sign that puberty has begun. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T6#GNS311_U1_T6_h4)

question: What is the main goal of using the 'teach-back' method when educating a patient?

options.A: To ensure the physician documented the correct diagnosis in the chart
options.B: To confirm that the patient truly understands the instructions in their own words
options.C: To test the patient's long-term memory after a neurological injury
options.D: To give the nurse a break from talking during the clinical consultation

explanation: Instead of asking 'Do you understand?' (where they'll just say yes), teach-back has them explain it back to you. It catches any misunderstandings instantly!

question: A patient with high cholesterol asks which fat to avoid completely. What should you tell them?

options.A: Trans fats
options.B: Omega-3 fatty acids
options.C: Polyunsaturated oils
options.D: Monounsaturated fats

explanation: Trans fats are artificial troublemakers! They raise bad cholesterol and lower the good kind, so it's best to avoid them for a healthy heart.

question: What makes an infant's upper airway much easier to block compared to an adult's?

options.A: A larger tongue relative to the oral cavity
options.B: A much wider trachea and larynx
options.C: Complete rigidity of the upper airway cartilage
options.D: An absence of mucus glands in the pharynx

explanation: Babies have surprisingly large tongues for their little mouths! If their head isn't positioned quite right, that tongue can easily slide back and block their airway.

question: What percentage of total blood volume is typically made up of plasma?

options.A: 45 percent
options.B: 20 percent
options.C: 55 percent
options.D: 80 percent

explanation: Plasma makes up about 55 percent of your blood. It acts as the liquid highway carrying cells, nutrients, and waste products all around the body!

question: Why is herd immunity so important for infants who are too young for certain vaccines?

options.A: It cures any congenital infections the infant was born with
options.B: It lowers the chance that the infant will encounter the infectious agent
options.C: It passes mature white blood cells directly through breast milk
options.D: It permanently removes all pathogens from the surrounding environment

explanation: You got it! When everyone around the baby is vaccinated, it builds a protective shield that keeps nasty germs far away from vulnerable little ones.

question: A patient just returned to the ward after a cerebral angiogram through the groin. What is a key nursing duty?

options.A: Checking the puncture site for bleeding and checking pulses below it
options.B: Restricting all drinking water for 24 hours
options.C: Removing the pressure bandage within the first ten minutes
options.D: Telling the patient to get up and walk around immediately

explanation: Always keep an eye on the puncture site and check the foot pulse to catch any bleeding or clotting early!

question: Which detail is most important to include in your notes when charting routine hair care?

options.A: The exact minute the hair drying process started
options.B: Condition of the scalp and any abnormal findings
options.C: The total cost of the hair care products used
options.D: The exact brand of shampoo preferred by the nurse

explanation: Always focus your documentation on clear clinical facts, such as how the scalp looks and any unusual signs you spot. [learn more](GNS112_U5_T5#GNS112_U5_T5_h6)

question: What is the main role of a home care nurse when working with the healthcare team on a slow-healing wound?

options.A: Acting as the eyes and ears to report accurate, up-to-date wound changes to providers
options.B: Ordering all prescription medications without physician approval
options.C: Performing surgical debridement during every home visit
options.D: Diagnosing the underlying systemic disease independently

explanation: You are the vital link! Your accurate updates from the home help doctors, dietitians, and specialists adjust the care plan so the patient heals faster.

question: Before you walk up to patients in a ward to chat with them for a study, what must you secure first?

options.A: Permission from the patient's family members only
options.B: A personal loan from the hospital bank
options.C: Formal institutional and ethical approval
options.D: Complete control over hospital bed assignments

explanation: You got it! Protecting patients is our number one priority. Ethical clearance is non-negotiable before any research begins.

question: A patient stands up fast and feels dizzy. What is the nurse likely suspecting?

options.A: Malignant hypertension
options.B: Acute hypoglycemia
options.C: Autonomic dysreflexia
options.D: Orthostatic hypotension

explanation: Spot on! That sudden drop in blood pressure when standing up is a classic sign of orthostatic hypotension after being on bed rest.

question: Which of these is NOT a classic sign of organophosphate (insecticide) poisoning?

options.A: Urinary incontinence
options.B: Extreme dryness of the skin
options.C: Watery eyes and diarrhea
options.D: Excessive salivation

explanation: Organophosphates throw the body's moisture switch into overdrive! Think watery eyes, drooling, and sweat—so the skin is definitely wet, never dry.

question: What is the primary type of tissue found in the hypodermis?

options.A: Nervous tissue
options.B: Stratified squamous tissue
options.C: Epithelial tissue
options.D: Adipose tissue

explanation: The hypodermis is heavily populated by fat-storing adipose cells that provide insulation and cushion underlying structures. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T1#GNS211_U2_T1_h4)

question: What is a common sign that a female patient has too much androgen in her system?

options.A: Permanent drop in core body temperature
options.B: Excessive facial hair growth and acne
options.C: Extreme softening of the fingernails
options.D: Sudden loss of all body hair

explanation: High androgens stimulate oil glands and hair follicles, which frequently leads to breakouts and unexpected hair growth patterns.

question: Why do barrier contraceptives usually have fewer medical restrictions than hormonal birth control pills?

options.A: They require a doctor to insert them every time
options.B: They do not change the body's hormone balance
options.C: They destroy all bacteria present in the vagina
options.D: They are completely 100 percent effective always

explanation: Exactly! Because barriers don't add synthetic hormones to the body, patients can avoid those systemic side effects. Great job!

question: Why should you avoid pouring harsh surgical scrubs directly inside an open wound?

options.A: It can damage exposed tissue cells and delay proper wound healing
options.B: It instantly inactivates any local anesthetic you inject later
options.C: It permanently stains the surrounding skin a bright yellow color
options.D: It causes the skin edges to swell up and prevent knot tying

explanation: Harsh chemicals are too strong for delicate exposed cells inside a wound. Stick to normal saline for cleaning—your patients will heal much better!

question: What is the medical term for the surgical removal of the gallbladder?

options.A: Cholecystectomy
options.B: Colectomy
options.C: Choledochotomy
options.D: Duodenostomy

explanation: You got it! A cholecystectomy is simply the surgical removal of the gallbladder, done either through tiny camera cuts or an open incision.

question: A patient has sharp, severe tummy pain that hurts much worse when they move or take a deep breath. What is the most likely cause?

options.A: Irritation of the parietal peritoneum
options.B: Slow movement in the large bowel
options.C: Normal gas movement through the colon
options.D: Stretching of a hollow organ muscle

explanation: The parietal peritoneum has lots of somatic nerve fibers that react sharply to movement and inflammation, causing that localized, sharp pain.

question: A patient asks why women get more bladder infections than men. What is the best anatomical reason to give?

options.A: Your urethra is much shorter, which makes it easier for bacteria to reach the bladder.
options.B: Women have weaker pelvic floor muscles that trap bacteria near the urinary opening.
options.C: The female bladder produces fewer protective enzymes than the male bladder.
options.D: Your body temperature creates a warmer environment for bacteria to multiply.

explanation: You're building strong clinical instincts! Because the female tube is short, bacteria have a much shorter distance to travel to cause an infection.

question: What is a major clinical advantage of Long-Acting Reversible Contraception (LARC) over regular daily pills?

options.A: They completely eliminate all risks of hormonal side effects
options.B: They do not rely on daily user adherence to remain effective
options.C: They can be inserted and removed safely at home by the patient
options.D: They provide automatic protection against viral and bacterial STIs

explanation: LARC methods (like implants or coils) take away the stress of remembering a daily pill. Once they're in, they work quietly in the background for years!

question: When is a syringe driver most likely to be used for a patient?

options.A: When the patient refuses all forms of nursing care
options.B: When intravenous access is completely forbidden by law
options.C: When the patient needs rapid blood pressure support
options.D: When oral medications are no longer safe or possible

explanation: Exactly! If a patient cannot swallow, has severe vomiting, or is nearing the end of life, a syringe driver is a lifesaver for giving regular medications smoothly.

question: What is the main goal of monitoring a patient after giving them a medication?

options.A: To calculate the total financial cost of the hospital stay
options.B: To evaluate therapeutic effectiveness and watch for adverse reactions
options.C: To write a long essay about the patient's medical history
options.D: To prove to hospital management that nurses are working hard

explanation: Checking on your patient later lets you see if the drug is actually working and helps you catch any side effects early.

question: Why do vulnerable population groups need special healthcare approaches instead of regular programs?

options.A: Government policy forbids them from visiting general clinics
options.B: They refuse to take any standard orthodox medications
options.C: They face unique barriers like poverty, isolation, and stigma
options.D: Standard programs are too expensive for hospitals to run

explanation: Spot on! Because of hurdles like distance, poverty, or discrimination, standard health programs often fail to reach them without special adjustments.

question: What simple comfort measure can a nurse suggest for a patient experiencing mild fibroid cramps?

options.A: Applying a heating pad to the lower abdomen
options.B: Drinking large quantities of ice-cold water
options.C: Lying completely flat on the back for hours
options.D: Engaging in high-impact aerobic exercise

explanation: Heat helps relax the tight uterine muscles, offering a wonderful, drug-free way to soothe mild cramping.

question: During which stage of HIV do patients often get a sudden spike in virus levels and flu-like signs?

options.A: Acute HIV infection
options.B: Clinical latency stage
options.C: Advanced AIDS stage
options.D: Terminal malignant stage

explanation: Spot on! The acute phase happens right after catching the virus, when the viral load shoots up and mild flu-like symptoms show up. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T2#GNS216_U6_T2_h4)

question: Which Nigerian agency is primarily responsible for enforcing environmental standards and regulations?

options.A: JAMB
options.B: NFF
options.C: NESREA
options.D: CBN

explanation: Correct! NESREA (National Environmental Standards and Regulations Enforcement Agency) keeps an eye on environmental compliance and pollution control across Nigeria.

question: Which intrapartum nursing action helps minimize the risk of vertical transmission during labor?

options.A: Performing frequent routine vaginal examinations
options.B: Encouraging immediate pushing during the early latent phase
options.C: Avoiding unnecessary artificial rupture of membranes
options.D: Administering oxytocin infusion to all mothers routinely

explanation: Keeping membranes intact as long as possible reduces the time the baby is exposed to infectious fluids in the birth canal. [learn more](GNS216_U6_T11#GNS216_U6_T11_h5)

question: Why do many cases of breast ironing go officially unrecorded in healthcare facilities?

options.A: Fear of cultural backlash and strict secrecy within communities
options.B: Patients naturally healing within a few days without scars
options.C: Direct government orders prohibiting doctors from asking about it
options.D: A complete absence of physical symptoms requiring medical care

explanation: Because family members enforce strict silence, victims rarely speak out due to intimidation and cultural norms. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T17#GNS312_U1_T17_h2)

question: Why is it important to check both physical health and mental status when assessing sexual problems?

options.A: Physical illnesses and emotional stress frequently interact to impair sexual function
options.B: Physical causes are always temporary while psychological ones are permanent
options.C: Medical insurance will not pay for treatment without both evaluations
options.D: Psychological causes can never be treated with medication

explanation: The body and mind work as a team. Good sexual health needs healthy blood vessels, steady hormones, and peace of mind all working together.

question: What is the primary focus of primary healthcare centers in Nigeria?

options.A: Basic preventive services and community health
options.B: Complex neurosurgeries and organ transplants
options.C: Long-term rehabilitation for chronic stroke
options.D: Advanced medical research and drug trials

explanation: Primary health centers handle grassroots care, immunizations, and treatment of common minor conditions. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T1#GNS112_U2_T1_h1)

question: During a surgical hand scrub, which way should the water drain off your arms?

options.A: From the elbows down toward the fingertips
options.B: Directly off the sides of the forearms
options.C: From the fingertips down toward the elbows
options.D: Upward toward the shoulders using towels

explanation: Always let water flow from your cleanest area (fingertips) down to your elbows. Gravity is your friend here!

question: Which of these is NOT something a bedside nurse is supposed to do during diagnostic tests?

options.A: Performing the official radiological interpretation of the scan
options.B: Monitoring the patient's vital signs throughout the procedure
options.C: Checking the insertion site for bleeding afterward
options.D: Verifying that informed consent has been obtained

explanation: Reading and officially interpreting scans is the job of trained radiologists or doctors, though nurses definitely watch for patient safety!

question: What stock rotation rule should be followed when storing sterile supplies?

options.A: Last-in, first-out
options.B: Random selection
options.C: First-in, first-out
options.D: Alphabetical order

explanation: Just like in a pharmacy or supermarket, 'First-In, First-Out' (FIFO) means older stock gets used first so nothing sits on the shelf long enough to expire.

question: A patient arrives at the emergency unit completely unresponsive after a road accident. Where should you get their health history?

options.A: Family members, emergency personnel, and previous medical records
options.B: Waiting until the patient wakes up before gathering any information
options.C: Guessing the past medical history based on the patient's age
options.D: Asking the patient's coworkers who are standing outside the room

explanation: Great job! When a patient can't speak for themselves, family members and past medical files are lifesavers for gathering background info.

question: When washing hands as a food handler, how long should you scrub with soap and water?

options.A: At least twenty seconds
options.B: Until they feel completely dry
options.C: Exactly five seconds
options.D: About two minutes

explanation: Good hygiene is our best shield! Scrubbing with soap for at least twenty seconds gives the soap enough time to lift away and destroy harmful germs.

question: A 10-day-old baby has mild eyelid swelling and watery discharge. Which germ is most likely the cause?

options.A: Neisseria gonorrhoeae
options.B: Silver nitrate drops
options.C: Escherichia coli
options.D: Chlamydia trachomatis

explanation: Spot on! Chlamydia tends to show up a bit later than gonorrhea—usually between 5 and 14 days after birth. You're building solid clinical instincts!

question: What common side effects should you warn a client about after taking hormonal emergency contraception?

options.A: Temporary nausea, headache, or irregular spotting
options.B: Sudden swelling of the lower limbs
options.C: Complete cessation of all future menstrual cycles
options.D: Permanent loss of vision in both eyes

explanation: A sudden rush of hormones can make clients feel a bit nauseous, tired, or give them a mild headache. Reassure them that this is totally normal and temporary!

question: Why are school-aged children especially prone to getting heavy worm infections?

options.A: Children have an increased biological requirement for adult worms
options.B: Stomach acid levels in children are too high for parasites to tolerate
options.C: Frequent outdoor play and hand-to-mouth behaviors increase exposure
options.D: Their immune systems permanently block all antihelminthic treatments

explanation: Kids love to play outside in the dirt, and with habits like putting unwashed hands in their mouths, they easily pick up parasite eggs.

question: How do drugs primarily work inside the human body?

options.A: They alter existing biological processes.
options.B: They create entirely new cellular functions.
options.C: They replace missing body organs permanently.
options.D: They destroy all pathogens without exception.

explanation: Think of medicines as assistants, not inventors! They don't create brand new body functions; they simply speed up or slow down things your body is already doing naturally. You've got this!

question: A woman at home experiences heavy vaginal bleeding shortly after delivering the placenta. What should the nurse do FIRST?

options.A: Send a family member to buy oral iron supplements from a local shop
options.B: Wait for thirty minutes to see if the bleeding stops on its own
options.C: Perform immediate uterine massage and administer oxytocin
options.D: Document the estimated blood loss in the register

explanation: Uterine massage and uterotonic drugs stimulate contractions to clamp down open blood vessels and stop the bleeding immediately. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T15#GNS324_U3_T15_h4)

question: A patient on chemo has a low platelet count. What should the nurse watch out for?

options.A: High fever and shaking chills
options.B: Swelling in the lower extremities
options.C: Yellow discoloration of the skin
options.D: Easy bruising and bleeding gums

explanation: Exactly! Platelets help blood clot. When they are low, simple things like brushing teeth can lead to bleeding gums or easy bruising.

question: How do safety checklists contribute to quality patient care in clinical practice?

options.A: They shorten the operating time for emergency surgeries
options.B: They automatically record the patient's vital signs into the computer
options.C: They replace the need for professional nursing judgment
options.D: They prevent the omission of critical steps during complex procedures

explanation: Checklists serve as memory aids to ensure that vital safety steps are never skipped during busy or high-stress procedures. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T1#GNS312_U5_T1_h7)

question: What is a key safety requirement for storing cleaning chemicals in a day care centre?

options.A: Storing them securely out of reach of children
options.B: Placing them next to food preparation counters
options.C: Keeping them unlocked on low shelves for easy access
options.D: Mixing them with drinking water for cleaning

explanation: Toxic chemicals must always be stored securely away from children to prevent accidental poisoning or chemical burns. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T7#GNS225_U4_T7_h4)

question: Which specific brain receptors do central anticholinergics block?

options.A: Opioid receptors
options.B: Adrenergic receptors
options.C: Nicotinic receptors
options.D: Muscarinic receptors

explanation: Central anticholinergics target and block muscarinic receptors to reduce cholinergic activity. [learn more](GNS223_U6_T7#GNS223_U6_T7_h2)

question: Which piece of personal protective equipment is put on last when preparing for a sterile procedure?

options.A: Cap
options.B: Gloves
options.C: Gown
options.D: Mask

explanation: Gloves are always donned last so they remain clean and do not touch other equipment during the gowning and masking process. [learn more](GNS311_U4_T1#GNS311_U4_T1_h5)

question: What is the main chemical trigger in your blood that tells your brain it is time to breathe?

options.A: Nitrogen gas dissolved in plasma
options.B: High levels of blood glucose
options.C: Carbon dioxide levels in the blood
options.D: Oxygen levels in the arterial blood

explanation: You got it! A buildup of carbon dioxide is the strongest alarm bell your body uses to say 'time to take a breath.'

question: What does REEDA stand for when a nurse checks a healing perineal wound?

options.A: Recovery, Examination, Epithelialization, Diameter, Assessment
options.B: Rubor, Erythema, Edema, Drainage, Alignment
options.C: Redness, Edema, Ecchymosis, Discharge, Approximation
options.D: Rate, Energy, Exudate, Depth, Area

explanation: You've got this! REEDA is our trusty clinical checklist to make sure a perineal tear or episiotomy is healing nicely without infection.

question: A patient has delivered two full-term babies, had one early miscarriage, and has two living children. What is her parity?

options.A: Three
options.B: Four
options.C: Two
options.D: Five

explanation: You've got this! Parity counts pregnancies that made it past 20 weeks (viable births). Since she had two full-term deliveries, her parity is 2.

question: What is the main purpose of a nursing shift handover on the ward?

options.A: To give doctors time to complete patient medical notes
options.B: To distribute weekly salaries to the nursing staff
options.C: To allow the hospital management to inspect ward cleanliness
options.D: To pass critical patient updates between incoming and outgoing staff

explanation: Handover ensures continuous, safe care by briefing the incoming shift on each patient's current status and needs. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T1#GNS112_U2_T1_h4)

question: If an intracardiac needle is placed too far to the side (laterally), which major organ might accidentally get punctured?

options.A: The kidneys
options.B: The pancreas
options.C: The lungs
options.D: The stomach

explanation: Great thinking! Because the lungs sit right next to the heart, pushing a needle too far sideways risks puncturing lung tissue and causing a collapse.

question: Why does atrophic gastritis often lead to vitamin B12 deficiency in older adults?

options.A: It speeds up the digestion of vitamins before the body can use them
options.B: It reduces stomach acid and intrinsic factor needed for absorption
options.C: It destroys the bacteria in the gut that naturally manufacture B12
options.D: It causes the liver to store less vitamin B12 than normal

explanation: Spot on! When stomach acid and intrinsic factor drop, the body struggles to break B12 away from food and absorb it in the gut. Great nursing insight to keep in mind!

question: Why is the right kidney positioned slightly lower in the abdomen than the left kidney?

options.A: The presence of the liver above it
options.B: A shorter right renal artery
options.C: The position of the spleen on the left
options.D: Greater muscle mass on the right side

explanation: The large right lobe of the liver pushes the right kidney slightly inferior compared to the left. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T1#GNS121_U2_T1_h1)

question: What is the primary definition of maternal morbidity in nursing practice?

options.A: Any health condition resulting from or worsened by pregnancy and childbirth
options.B: The permanent inability to conceive after experiencing a miscarriage
options.C: Any psychological stress experienced immediately after delivering a baby
options.D: The total number of maternal deaths recorded in a specific community

explanation: Maternal morbidity covers any physical or mental condition that affects a woman because of pregnancy, childbirth, or the postpartum period, short of death itself. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T001#GNS226_U5_T001_h1)

question: Why do proton pumps in the collecting duct rely on primary active transport?

options.A: To push hydrogen ions against a very steep concentration gradient
options.B: To reabsorb all filtered glucose before it reaches the bladder
options.C: To prevent potassium from entering the urine under normal conditions
options.D: To move sodium ions passively alongside water molecules

explanation: Because the urine is already packed with acid, pushing more hydrogen ions in takes extra energy. That's why primary active transport uses direct energy to get the job done!

question: For a stroke patient with left-sided weakness who is confined to bed, what is the best nursing action to prevent bedsores?

options.A: Keeping the head of the bed completely flat at all times
options.B: Repositioning the patient every two hours and supporting weak limbs
options.C: Restricting oral fluid intake to keep the skin dry
options.D: Massaging the reddened bony prominences vigorously every shift

explanation: You nailed it! Turning the patient regularly relieves pressure on vulnerable skin, while supporting weak limbs protects their joints.

question: A patient with a severe bone infection is losing weight rapidly despite resting in bed all day. What is the main reason for this?

options.A: Infections make the patient drink too much water instead of eating.
options.B: The patient's liver is storing too much fat for future use.
options.C: The body is in a breakdown state, using its own tissues for extra energy.
options.D: Bed rest causes the stomach to stop digesting food completely.

explanation: Severe illness triggers catabolism, where the body breaks down muscle and fat to meet the high energy demands of fighting the disease. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T023#GNS227_U2_T023_h2)

question: Besides physical treatment, what else is an essential part of holistic post-abortion care?

options.A: Mandatory reporting of the client to local religious leaders
options.B: Empathetic emotional support and contraceptive counseling
options.C: Permanent hospital admission for psychological observation
options.D: Informing the client's family members about the medical history

explanation: Good nursing looks at the whole person! Along with healing the body, we offer kind emotional support and teach them about family planning for the future.

question: How does an occupational therapist mostly differ from a physiotherapist?

options.A: Occupational therapists focus on adapting practical daily life tasks and home environments
options.B: Occupational therapists only work in intensive care units
options.C: Occupational therapists are licensed to prescribe medications
options.D: Occupational therapists deal exclusively with mental health disorders

explanation: While physiotherapists focus on body movement and strength, occupational therapists help patients master everyday chores like cooking, washing, and dressing.

question: How does drug absorption in the lower rectum affect metabolism?

options.A: It sends all medications directly to the stomach
options.B: It destroys the active ingredients instantly
options.C: It forces the drug to be stored in the kidneys
options.D: It bypasses the liver's first-pass metabolism

explanation: Lower rectal veins carry the drug straight into the general circulation, skipping the quick breakdown by the liver that oral pills face.

question: What is the main force that pushes the baby down during the first stage of labour?

options.A: Voluntary maternal abdominal pushing
options.B: Intermittent uterine contractions
options.C: Gravity pulling the fetus downward
options.D: Manual traction by the midwife

explanation: You've got this! Uterine contractions do the heavy lifting to open the cervix and push the baby down even before the mother starts pushing.

question: What important detail must be included when documenting an intradermal injection?

options.A: Brand name of the alcohol swab
options.B: Name of the nurse's supervisor
options.C: Patient's favorite arm preference
options.D: Exact anatomical site used

explanation: Recording the exact location is necessary so the healthcare team can find the correct spot when returning to read the test results. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T6#GNS122_U1_T6_h7)

question: What big problem can happen with combined city sewer systems during heavy rainstorms?

options.A: Electrical pumps inside homes automatically reverse their flow
options.B: The municipal water pressure drops to zero across the entire city
options.C: Overflows can dump raw, untreated sewage directly into natural water bodies
options.D: Underground pipes freeze solid because of rapid temperature drops

explanation: When storm water and sewage share the same pipes, heavy rains can easily overwhelm the system. When this happens, raw, untreated waste spills straight into local rivers or lakes.

question: You check a new mother and notice her uterus feels soft and is pushed over to the right side. What should you do first?

options.A: Assist the patient to empty her bladder
options.B: Massage the calves to prevent clots
options.C: Administer a blood transfusion immediately
options.D: Encourage heavy ambulation around the ward

explanation: A full bladder acts like a bully, pushing the uterus upward and to the side and stopping it from contracting properly. Helping her pee often fixes the problem instantly! Great nursing intuition. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T016#GNS226_U3_T016_h3)

question: A client looks in the mirror after an EEG and feels upset because their hair is messy with sticky paste. What is the best nursing action?

options.A: Help the client wash their hair with warm water and shampoo
options.B: Ask the physician to write an order for a scalp scrub
options.C: Apply rubbing alcohol to dissolve the paste quickly
options.D: Tell the client the paste will wash off on its own tomorrow

explanation: That electrode paste can be super sticky and stubborn! Helping the patient clean up shows great bedside manner and restores their comfort.

question: What is the most common reason clients stop using their birth control method?

options.A: Forgetting clinic locations
options.B: Traveling out of the country
options.C: Experiencing side effects
options.D: Changing religious beliefs

explanation: When clients face physical or emotional side effects that they don't know how to handle, they usually stop using the method.

question: What is the main benefit of keeping accurate records of workplace injuries and close calls?

options.A: It helps identify dangerous trends and prevents future accidents
options.B: It guarantees that the business will never face taxation
options.C: It allows employers to hide safety violations from inspectors
options.D: It replaces the need to provide medical treatment to victims

explanation: Reviewing past injury logs helps safety teams spot repeating problems so they can fix them before anyone else gets hurt.

question: How do vaccines work to protect a child's body against infections?

options.A: By stimulating the immune system to produce antibodies
options.B: By coating the stomach lining to block germ absorption
options.C: By increasing the body temperature to kill viruses
options.D: By providing immediate chemical destruction of all bacteria

explanation: Exactly! Vaccines introduce safe, weakened parts of a germ to train the immune system so it knows how to fight back if the real disease ever shows up.

question: Why is proper cleaning of the urethral meatus required before collecting a clean-catch urine sample?

options.A: To decrease burning sensations caused by dysuria during the collection
options.B: To stimulate the bladder muscles and encourage full voiding
options.C: To prevent bacteria from the skin from contaminating the urine culture
options.D: To ensure the specific gravity remains within normal limits

explanation: Skin flora can easily enter the urine stream during collection, leading to false-positive culture results. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T2#GNS213_U4_T2_h4)

question: A ward manager notices more patient falls happening. What should they do right after gathering this data?

options.A: Write a brand new job description for the ward clerk
options.B: Ignore the data until the end of the fiscal year audit
options.C: Compare the fall rates against the established hospital safety benchmark
options.D: Immediately fire the nurses working the night shift without investigation

explanation: Once you collect the data, the logical next step is to compare it to your hospital's safety standard to see how big the gap is.

question: Which baby health problems are most common when born to teenage mothers?

options.A: Congenital heart murmurs caused by maternal stress
options.B: Advanced bone maturation at birth
options.C: Premature birth and low birth weight
options.D: Excessive birth weight and overgrown organs

explanation: Spot on! Because the mother's body is still growing, babies often arrive too early and small.

question: How do transactional leaders mainly manage their staff?

options.A: Democratic voting on every single hospital policy
options.B: A system of rewards and corrective actions
options.C: Deep emotional bonding and shared spiritual visions
options.D: Complete freedom with zero performance tracking

explanation: Transactional leadership works like a clear exchange: do well and get rewarded, make a mistake or slack off and face corrections.

question: Why do we bother grouping drugs into different classes?

options.A: To eliminate the need for nurses to check patient vital signs
options.B: To dictate the exact financial cost of each medication in the pharmacy
options.C: To ensure that every drug has exactly one trade name worldwide
options.D: To group medications with similar properties and manage vast pharmaceutical knowledge

explanation: You're right on track! There are thousands of drugs out there, and classification helps us make sense of them by grouping similar ones together.

question: Why are patients with nephrotic syndrome at a much higher risk for blood clots?

options.A: They lie in bed all day without moving their legs
options.B: Their red blood cell count increases drastically
options.C: They lose clotting-regulatory proteins through their urine
options.D: Their blood pressure is always extremely high

explanation: The kidneys filter out proteins that normally prevent blood from clotting too easily, leaving the blood in a hypercoagulable state. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T8#GNS213_U4_T8_h6)

question: Why is a severely low-protein diet generally discouraged for patients with nephrotic syndrome?

options.A: It makes the urine completely stop flowing
options.B: It increases the risk of developing diabetes mellitus
options.C: It causes blood pressure to rise to dangerous levels
options.D: It does not stop protein loss and can lead to muscle breakdown

explanation: Don't worry if this tripped you up! Restricting protein doesn't stop the kidneys from leaking it; instead, it starves the patient's body and leads to muscle wasting.

question: What is one of the most common causes of medication errors on a busy hospital ward?

options.A: Distractions and interruptions during preparation
options.B: Writing patient names clearly in black ink
options.C: Performing three checks against the prescription order
options.D: Asking patients to state their date of birth

explanation: Noise and interruptions break your focus. When drawing up meds or checking doses, try to find a quiet zone to avoid silly mistakes!

question: Which healthcare worker usually acts as the central link for the team because they spend the most time at the bedside?

options.A: The consulting surgeon
options.B: The registered nurse
options.C: The hospital pharmacist
options.D: The financial administrator

explanation: Spot on! Because nurses are always close to the patient, they are in the best position to spot changes and coordinate care.

question: During a home visit, you notice the weights for a patient's skin traction are resting on the floor. What is your very first action?

options.A: Document that the patient is non-compliant with bedrest orders
options.B: Remove the traction setup entirely because it is no longer effective
options.C: Ensure the weights hang freely without touching the floor or bed
options.D: Add extra weight to make up for the time the weights spent resting

explanation: Traction weights must always hang free! If they touch the floor, the pulling force stops, and the bones won't stay aligned.

question: During a pediatric resuscitation, how often should epinephrine be given?

options.A: Only after five defibrillation shocks
options.B: Every 3 to 5 minutes
options.C: Once every hour
options.D: Every 30 seconds

explanation: Epinephrine is a trusty emergency medication given every 3 to 5 minutes during a code to help keep blood flowing to the heart and brain.

question: What is your top assessment priority when caring for a patient with a severe lung infection?

options.A: Measuring the belly size every four hours
options.B: Checking reflexes in the legs
options.C: Checking for swollen feet
options.D: Monitoring breathing rate, depth, and oxygen levels

explanation: Respiratory status comes first! Keeping a close eye on breathing and oxygen saturation helps you catch any sudden downturn early.

question: How do nurse-led community outreach programs help improve maternal health in rural Nigeria?

options.A: By educating families and encouraging them to seek care at health facilities
options.B: By providing free vehicles to every pregnant woman in the village
options.C: By replacing the need for doctors and hospitals in all situations
options.D: By banning traditional birth attendants from practicing entirely

explanation: Outreach bridges the gap! By teaching families to spot danger signs, we help them get to the clinic early when help is most effective. [learn more](GNS226_U1_T003#GNS226_U1_T003_h8)

question: How do you measure the correct insertion length for a nasogastric tube?

options.A: From the mouth straight down to the knee
options.B: From the center of the chest to the wrist
options.C: From the forehead down to the belly button
options.D: From nose to earlobe to xiphoid process

explanation: This classic anatomical landmark measurement ensures the tip of the tube reaches safely inside the stomach cavity. [learn more](GNS213_U3_T3#GNS213_U3_T3_h4)

question: Why is watching a patient actually do a household task better than just asking if they can do it?

options.A: Patients often lie to nurses to avoid being sent away to a hospital.
options.B: Verbal reports may not match the patient's actual physical capability.
options.C: Patients forget the names of the tools they use for cooking and cleaning.
options.D: Direct observation is a mandatory legal requirement in all provinces.

explanation: Spot on! People often overestimate what they can do or try to hide their struggles, so watching them yourself gives you the true picture.

question: Which body parts are included in the appendicular region?

options.A: Thorax and abdomen
options.B: Spine and pelvis
options.C: Upper and lower limbs
options.D: Head and neck

explanation: The appendicular region contains all the bones and soft tissues of the upper and lower extremities. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T4#GNS111_U1_T4_h3)

question: Which cranial nerve controls the muscles for chewing and lets you feel sensations on your face?

options.A: Olfactory nerve
options.B: Hypoglossal nerve
options.C: Trochlear nerve
options.D: Trigeminal nerve

explanation: Cranial Nerve V (the trigeminal nerve) is responsible for feeling things on your face and helping you chew your food.

question: A nurse puts a patient with a severe cough in a private room. Which part of the chain of infection is the nurse mainly controlling?

options.A: Infectious dose and incubation period
options.B: Reservoir and portal of exit
options.C: Environmental temperature and humidity
options.D: Portal of entry and susceptibility

explanation: By isolating the patient, you trap the human reservoir and block the germs from escaping into the ward air!

question: When is an emergency caesarean section a must instead of giving drugs to speed up labour?

options.A: When the cervix is four centimetres dilated
options.B: When the mother feels mild fatigue
options.C: When membranes rupture spontaneously
options.D: When cephalopelvic disproportion is present

explanation: If the pelvis is too small for the baby (CPD), giving drugs to force contractions would be very dangerous and could cause the uterus to rupture. Surgery is life-saving here!

question: A patient has a worm infection. Which white blood cell count will likely be high on their lab results?

options.A: Eosinophils
options.B: Platelets
options.C: Erythrocytes
options.D: Neutrophils

explanation: Correct! Eosinophils are the specialists specialized in fighting off parasites and calming down allergic reactions.

question: What is the main purpose of a referral pathway in humanitarian GBV response?

options.A: To ensure that nurses do not have to provide any clinical treatment
options.B: To force every patient to repeat their traumatic story to multiple agencies
options.C: To transfer patient debt records to international banking organizations
options.D: To connect survivors with coordinated medical, legal, and shelter services

explanation: A referral pathway links different support groups together so the patient gets total care without missing steps or getting bounced around blindly.

question: What is the primary goal of a descriptive cross-sectional study?

options.A: To follow patients from birth until old age
options.B: To prove that one factor causes another over time
options.C: To show how common a health condition is in a population
options.D: To test the effectiveness of a new surgical tool

explanation: Descriptive studies simply lay out the facts—like how widespread a condition is—without trying to prove cause and effect.

question: What is a major barrier that prevents teenagers from visiting clinics for contraceptives?

options.A: The high academic performance required to enter clinics
options.B: Mandatory free transport provided to all school children
options.C: A complete absence of any illness during adolescence
options.D: Fear of judgmental staff and lack of confidentiality

explanation: Many teens avoid clinics because they fear being scolded by healthcare workers or having their visits reported to their parents. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T9#GNS312_U3_T9_h8)

question: Which of these is NOT a good way to stop drug theft in a pharmacy store?

options.A: Conducting surprise physical counts of valuable medicines
options.B: Installing security cameras around the dispensing counters
options.C: Restricting key access to authorized storekeepers only
options.D: Leaving the main storage room unlocked during lunch breaks

explanation: Leaving storage rooms unlocked is an open invitation for missing inventory! Security requires locked doors and controlled access.

question: Which specific medication is used to treat encephalitis caused by the herpes simplex virus?

options.A: Acyclovir
options.B: Ibuprofen
options.C: Penicillin
options.D: Fluconazole

explanation: Acyclovir is our go-to antiviral medication for herpes virus infections, including nasty cases of viral encephalitis. You'll see this drug very often in clinical practice!

question: In the epidemiological triangle, what does the 'host' refer to?

options.A: The human or animal that carries the infectious organism
options.B: The specific microorganism causing the sickness
options.C: The medication used to treat the infection
options.D: The physical climate where the outbreak takes place

explanation: Spot on! The host is simply the living creature—like you, me, or an animal—that provides a home for the disease-causing germ.

question: What is the primary purpose of a community health nursing care plan?

options.A: To replace all medical textbooks used in nursing schools
options.B: To punish community members who break environmental laws
options.C: To guide practical nursing actions and measure health outcomes
options.D: To serve as a decoration for the office wall of the clinic head

explanation: A care plan is your step-by-step roadmap. It tells you what actions to take, who is responsible, and how to check if things are getting better.

question: What is the biggest risk of trying to estimate your injection usage from memory?

options.A: It automatically invalidates the nurse's practicing license
options.B: It causes immediate physical damage to safety boxes
options.C: It doubles the financial cost of purchasing new syringes
options.D: It distorts supply chain forecasts and leads to future stockouts

explanation: Spot on! If our recorded guesses are wrong, the central store will send the wrong quantity, leading to frustrating shortages.

question: What is pica, a condition nurses watch out for during dietary checks?

options.A: An allergic reaction to eating citrus fruits during pregnancy
options.B: An excessive thirst that leads to drinking too much water daily
options.C: A complete loss of appetite caused by severe hormonal changes
options.D: A strong craving to eat non-food items like clay, starch, or ice

explanation: Pica happens when a mum craves non-food items like chalk or clay. It's usually the body's way of whispering that she lacks certain minerals like iron!

question: What immediate lab test must be done before giving a blood transfusion to a severely anaemic labor patient?

options.A: Complete metabolic panel
options.B: Clotting profile
options.C: Urinalysis culture
options.D: Type and crossmatch

explanation: Safety first! Typing and crossmatching ensure the donated blood matches the patient and won't cause a dangerous reaction.

question: A patient with a progressive neurological disorder starts having trouble swallowing and controlling their bladder. What do we call this type of issue?

options.A: Acute infection
options.B: Sensory overload
options.C: Autonomic dysfunction
options.D: Cerebellar excitation

explanation: The autonomic nervous system handles automatic body jobs like swallowing, digestion, and bladder control. When it gets impaired, these tricky symptoms show up. You're mastering patient assessment!

question: What is the main focus of a geriatrician compared to a general doctor?

options.A: Providing nursing care in community health clinics
options.B: Specialized training in the unique health conditions of older adults
options.C: Exclusive focus on surgical procedures for the elderly
options.D: Managing hospital finances and bed allocations

explanation: Geriatricians take extra time to study how aging, chronic illnesses, and multiple medications all interact in older bodies.

question: What is the main goal of community-based rehabilitation programs in developing regions?

options.A: To eliminate the need for trained nurses and therapists
options.B: To replace all acute hospital medical care with home remedies
options.C: To bring rehabilitation services closer to local homes and families
options.D: To isolate disabled individuals inside specialized urban centers

explanation: Community-based care bridges the gap by bringing help directly to people in their local neighborhoods where specialized hospitals might be far away.

question: You gently pinch an elderly patient's forearm skin and notice it stays tented up for a few seconds before going down. What does this mean?

options.A: Dehydration or reduced skin elasticity
options.B: Excessive fluid retention in the subcutaneous tissue
options.C: Severe local skin inflammation or infection
options.D: Normal physiological response to warm ambient air

explanation: When skin stays up after pinching (poor turgor), it's a classic sign of low fluid levels (dehydration) or normal aging changes.

question: Where should you position the steam generator in relation to the patient's bed?

options.A: Underneath the mattress for hidden warmth
options.B: Tied securely to the side rail of the crib
options.C: At a safe distance to prevent accidental burns
options.D: Directly inside the tent canopy next to the pillow

explanation: Safety first! Always keep the hot generator far enough away to protect the patient from burns.

question: Which of these options is NOT a secondary sexual characteristic?

options.A: A deeper vocal pitch
options.B: Facial hair growth
options.C: The uterus and ovaries
options.D: Enlarged breast tissue

explanation: Correct! The uterus and ovaries are primary sex organs (we are born with them), while secondary characteristics develop later on the outside.

question: Why is it important for a clinical nurse to know about health maintenance agencies?

options.A: Agency guidelines dictate daily hospital protocols and safety standards
options.B: Nurses must directly fund these large government organizations
options.C: Hospital accreditation depends entirely on individual patient tips
options.D: Clinical nurses are legally required to manage agency budgets

explanation: Spot on! The rules, safety protocols, and daily routines we follow in the wards come directly from these health agencies.

question: Which of the following is a classic example of an Activity of Daily Living (ADL)?

options.A: Managing household financial accounts
options.B: Driving a car to the grocery store
options.C: Preparing a hot meal on the stove
options.D: Eating a meal independently

explanation: ADLs are the fundamental things we do every day to care for ourselves, like eating, bathing, dressing, and walking around.

question: How do drug name stems help a student nurse understand unfamiliar medications?

options.A: They show the exact expiration date and proper storage temperature needed
options.B: They tell the nurse the exact retail price of the medication in the pharmacy
options.C: Common suffixes reveal the pharmacological class and general action of the drug
options.D: They indicate which manufacturing company produced the specific batch of pills

explanation: Drug stems (like '-olol' for beta-blockers) are like cheat codes! They tell you what family a drug belongs to, helping you guess its action even if you've never seen it before.

question: A patient is diagnosed with glaucoma caused by blocked fluid drainage in the front of the eye. What fluid is building up?

options.A: Blood plasma
options.B: Lacrimal fluid
options.C: Vitreous humor
options.D: Aqueous humor

explanation: Aqueous humor is the watery fluid in the anterior segment whose blockage leads to increased pressure in glaucoma. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T1#GNS211_U4_T1_h3)

question: What is the main goal of a Drug Revolving Fund (DRF) in a hospital?

options.A: To ensure a steady and uninterrupted supply of essential medicines
options.B: To provide free medical treatments to all vulnerable populations
options.C: To pay the monthly salaries of clinical and administrative staff
options.D: To generate excess profit for hospital infrastructure development

explanation: Spot on! The DRF is like a rolling fund. Money from drug sales goes right back into buying more drugs so the pharmacy never runs empty.

question: Why is performing FGM in a modern hospital still considered unacceptable?

options.A: It breaks medical ethics and human rights regardless of hygiene
options.B: It costs too much money for the local community
options.C: Hospitals lack the proper tools for cutting female genitalia
options.D: Modern medicine cannot stop the bleeding from FGM

explanation: A clean environment does not erase the severe physical and psychological trauma or the breach of medical ethics. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T5#GNS312_U1_T5_h1)

question: By what age does a typical infant double their birth weight?

options.A: Six months
options.B: Nine months
options.C: Three months
options.D: Twelve months

explanation: Infants generally double their birth weight by six months of age and triple it by twelve months. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T12#GNS324_U3_T12_h2)

question: Which of these is a common challenge that ruins a good nursing handover?

options.A: Using the SBAR framework correctly
options.B: Noise, distractions, and staff fatigue
options.C: Having too many standardized reporting templates
options.D: Patients being fully awake and cooperative

explanation: When people are tired and the ward is noisy, it's super easy to miss crucial details during report.

question: Which specific antidote is given to protect the liver during a dangerous paracetamol (acetaminophen) overdose?

options.A: Flumazenil
options.B: Naloxone
options.C: Atropine
options.D: N-acetylcysteine

explanation: N-acetylcysteine is a lifesaver here! It replenishes a vital liver chemical (glutathione) and stops paracetamol byproducts from destroying the liver tissue.

question: What happens to disease prevalence if a new, highly effective cure is discovered?

options.A: Prevalence doubles because more people will seek testing
options.B: Prevalence increases because cured patients are counted twice
options.C: Prevalence stays the same because cures do not affect statistics
options.D: Prevalence decreases because patients recover and leave the active pool

explanation: Quick recovery removes people from the count of existing cases, driving the prevalence rate down. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T12#GNS313_U1_T12_h4)

question: What happens inside lung cells when beta-2 receptors are stimulated?

options.A: An increase in intracellular cyclic AMP
options.B: The immediate destruction of lung tissue
options.C: A massive influx of calcium into the cell
options.D: A sudden drop in systemic blood pressure

explanation: When beta-2 receptors are activated, they trigger a messenger called cyclic AMP (cAMP) inside the cell. This is the secret step that tells the airway muscles to relax!

question: A patient receives several bags of packed red blood cells after an accident, but no plasma. What clotting complication are they most at risk for?

options.A: Vitamin K toxicity
options.B: Dilutive coagulopathy
options.C: Hereditary hemophilia A
options.D: Polycythemia vera

explanation: If you only pump in red blood cells without replacing plasma, you end up diluting the patient's remaining platelets and clotting factors. This is called dilutive coagulopathy.

question: What smart strategy helps protect a DRF against rising market prices?

options.A: Periodic and responsible review of drug selling prices
options.B: Giving free credit to all patients who request it
options.C: Stopping the purchase of expensive imported medications
options.D: Selling all essential drugs at a 90% discount

explanation: Adjusting prices sensibly helps the fund keep up with replacement costs so the pharmacy never runs dry.

question: How do abdominal thrusts (the Heimlich maneuver) help a choking person?

options.A: They drain trapped fluid from the lower lungs
options.B: They force trapped air upward to pop the object out
options.C: They help the heart pump blood faster
options.D: They help the patient relax their vocal cords

explanation: Abdominal thrusts squeeze the diaphragm upward. This creates a quick puff of artificial air from the lungs that acts like a cough to push the blockage out.

question: What is the first blood collection step when performing a standard GTT?

options.A: Drawing blood immediately after drinking the glucose drink
options.B: Drawing a baseline fasting blood sample
options.C: Waiting two hours before taking any blood sample
options.D: Checking urine glucose before touching the patient

explanation: A fasting blood sample must always be collected first to establish the patient's baseline glucose level before giving the drink. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T20#GNS222_U2_T20_h4)

question: What is a common sign you might notice if you are breathing in small amounts of leaking theater anaesthetic gas over a long time?

options.A: Permanent hearing loss
options.B: Sudden bone fractures
options.C: Your hair starts growing way too fast
options.D: Headaches and feeling sleepy

explanation: When theatre rooms aren't well ventilated, breathing in low levels of escaping gases over time often triggers headaches, fatigue, and drowsiness.

question: Why is priority setting such an important step in community health nursing?

options.A: Health laws prohibit nurses from tackling more than one disease
options.B: Most communities only ever experience a single health issue
options.C: It ensures that minor problems are always treated before major ones
options.D: Resources are never enough to solve every health problem at once

explanation: Exactly! Because time, money, and staff are always limited, we have to prioritize which issues need our immediate attention.

question: A stroke patient has weak arms on one side, but she can still wash her face if her wash basin is placed close by. What should you do?

options.A: Tell her family to do all her bathing when they visit
options.B: Wait until her full strength returns before she bathes
options.C: Encourage her to wash her upper body while you assist with the rest
options.D: Do everything for her to save her energy

explanation: Wonderful choice! Encouraging whatever independence a patient has left boosts their mood and helps them recover faster.

question: Why might a patient with severe carbon monoxide poisoning show a falsely normal or high oxygen saturation reading on a pulse oximeter?

options.A: Carbon monoxide makes the pulse rate extremely fast
options.B: Cold fingers stop the machine from recording low numbers
options.C: Bright lights in the room interfere with the infrared sensors
options.D: The device reads carbon monoxide attached to hemoglobin just like oxygen

explanation: Standard pulse oximeters cannot distinguish between oxygen and carbon monoxide bound to hemoglobin, leading to dangerously misleading high readings. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T6#GNS212_U4_T6_h7)

question: What is the main goal of primary prevention?

options.A: Rehabilitating a patient after major cancer surgery
options.B: Catching an existing disease during its very early stages
options.C: Providing palliative comfort during end-of-life care
options.D: Preventing a disease from ever occurring in a healthy person

explanation: Think of primary prevention as stopping trouble before it even starts—like protecting healthy people by reducing risk factors.

question: A community nurse is running an antenatal class. Which of these shows great community nutrition promotion?

options.A: Advising mothers to avoid all local market vegetables for safety reasons
options.B: Distributing recipes that require specialized cooking equipment from abroad
options.C: Explaining complex biochemical pathways of vitamins to pregnant women
options.D: Teaching mothers how to combine local beans and grains for better protein value

explanation: You nailed it! Showing mothers how to creatively mix everyday local ingredients empowers them to take charge of their family's health.

question: An emergency patient needs medicine right now. Which route will work the fastest?

options.A: Intravenous
options.B: Topical cream
options.C: Oral capsule
options.D: Subcutaneous

explanation: You got it! IV is the champion for speed during emergencies because it enters the blood instantly.

question: Why should you never make a patient vomit after they have swallowed a strong acid?

options.A: It forces the acid to enter the bloodstream through the lungs
options.B: It neutralizes the stomach acid so fast that the heart stops
options.C: It prevents medical personnel from ever identifying the poison
options.D: It causes the corrosive chemical to damage the esophagus a second time

explanation: Excellent clinical instinct! Bringing the acid back up forces it to burn the delicate lining of the throat and mouth all over again, making the injury much worse.

question: Why is it important for a nurse to tell a patient about the loud noises an MRI machine makes?

options.A: To prevent sudden panic or movement during the test
options.B: To prove that the computer system is working correctly
options.C: To help the patient choose the right size of earplugs
options.D: To ensure the patient speaks loudly through the intercom

explanation: Unexpected loud noises can startle a patient, causing them to jump or move, which ruins the image quality and requires a restart. [learn more](GNS123_U2_T12#GNS123_U2_T12_h5)

question: Which part of the female reproductive organ is affected by cervical cancer?

options.A: The lower part of the uterus
options.B: The external folds of the labia majora
options.C: The muscular walls of the fallopian tubes
options.D: The inner lining of the ovarian cortex

explanation: Great job! Cervical cancer happens right in the cervix, which is the lower, narrow neck of the uterus connecting to the vagina. You've got this!

question: A family caregiver looks very tired and says they can't sleep because of worry over night medications. What should you do?

options.A: Assess caregiver strain and explore local support or respite options
options.B: Discharge the patient immediately due to unreliable family support
options.C: Advise the patient to manage all nighttime medications alone
options.D: Tell the family member that burnout is simply part of being a caregiver

explanation: You got it! Caregiver fatigue is real. Checking on their well-being and finding support helps keep home care safe and sustainable.

question: A patient complains of a warm, sharp-feeling joint after physical therapy. What is your best nursing action?

options.A: Apply a cold pack to the joint and encourage rest
options.B: Administer a double dose of oral antibiotics immediately
options.C: Apply a warm moist towel to increase blood flow further
options.D: Encourage immediate heavy resistance exercises to push through

explanation: Cold packs are great for calming down a hot, angry joint. They narrow blood vessels, drop acute inflammation, and soothe sharp pain.

question: A male patient insists he doesn't have an STI because his sores don't hurt. How should you gently correct him?

options.A: Painlessness proves that the infection is restricted to the skin surface only
options.B: Some serious infections like syphilis can cause painless sores in their early stages
options.C: If a lesion does not hurt, the body will eliminate the virus automatically
options.D: Painless sores always indicate a non-infectious skin allergy rather than an STI

explanation: It's a common trap! Remind your patients that a lack of pain does not mean lack of disease—syphilis chancres are notorious for being painless.

question: Which nursing action helps a hospitalized patient cough up thick mucus more easily?

options.A: Encouraging fluids and deep breathing exercises
options.B: Keeping the patient lying flat in bed all day
options.C: Restricting water to prevent fluid buildup in the lungs
options.D: Giving strong sleeping pills to stop the cough

explanation: Water is a natural thinner for mucus! Combined with deep breathing and controlled coughing, it helps clear the airways safely.

question: While in the ambulance, you notice the intravenous (IV) line has stopped flowing. What is the very first thing you should check?

options.A: Whether the tubing is kinked or the patient's arm is bent
options.B: Whether the patient's blood type needs to be re-checked
options.C: Whether the ambulance driver is speeding too fast
options.D: Whether the hospital pharmacy has more fluid in stock

explanation: Great clinical thinking! Movement in transit often causes IV tubing to bend or kink. Always check the line physically first.

question: What do we call a small drug molecule that joins with body proteins to trigger an immune response?

options.A: An antibody
options.B: An electrolyte
options.C: A hormone
options.D: A hapten

explanation: A hapten is like a tiny hitchhiker! It's too small on its own to bother the immune system, but once it attaches to a larger body protein, the immune system notices and reacts.

question: What is an essential first step for a nurse providing effective sexual health advocacy?

options.A: Overcoming personal discomfort and professional biases
options.B: Referring every patient directly to a psychiatric hospital
options.C: Writing research papers on rare reproductive diseases
options.D: Requiring patients to sign a formal intimacy contract

explanation: Nurses must first address their own biases and discomfort to create a safe, welcoming environment for their patients. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T26#GNS312_U1_T26_h8)

question: Why does our sense of taste naturally react strongly against bitter foods?

options.A: To identify energy-rich carbohydrate sources
options.B: To maintain normal blood electrolyte levels
options.C: To signal the presence of dietary protein
options.D: To warn the body against potential poisons

explanation: Think of bitterness as your body's built-in alarm system! It evolved to help us spot dangerous toxins or plant alkaloids before we swallow them.

question: Which common Nigerian food is a great plant-based source of protein?

options.A: Cassava tubers
options.B: Cowpeas (beans)
options.C: White yam slices
options.D: Ripe plantain fruits

explanation: Beans (cowpeas) are a fantastic, affordable local source of plant protein that helps build and repair body tissues.

question: Which action is considered the single most effective way to prevent the spread of infections in a healthcare setting?

options.A: Keeping windows closed at night
options.B: Painting isolation walls white
options.C: Frequent and proper hand hygiene
options.D: Changing bed sheets twice a day

explanation: Handwashing with soap and water or using alcohol-based rub removes pathogens from hands before they spread to others. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T5#GNS123_U4_T5_h7)

question: Why must nurses be careful when reading antibody blood tests for an active infection?

options.A: Antibodies only work when the patient has a high fever
options.B: Antibodies can stick around in the blood long after an old infection is gone
options.C: Antibodies change shape daily inside the human bloodstream
options.D: Antibodies destroy the laboratory testing equipment if left too long

explanation: Well done! Because our immune system remembers past fights, a positive antibody test might just mean an old infection, not a current one.

question: Why do nurses always tell patients to take levothyroxine on an empty stomach?

options.A: Food neutralizes the stomach acid needed to activate the tablet
options.B: Food and certain minerals in the gut can reduce the drug's absorption
options.C: The drug causes severe stomach ulcers if mixed with food proteins
options.D: Taking it with food causes immediate destruction of the liver

explanation: Things like calcium, iron, and heavy meals can trap the drug in your gut and stop it from getting into your bloodstream where it's needed.

question: Why do nurses use the four-quadrant method during a quick abdominal assessment?

options.A: To quickly locate the general area of organ pain or discomfort
options.B: To determine the patient's daily fluid intake requirements
options.C: To calculate the exact surface area of the skin in square centimeters
options.D: To measure muscle strength in the lower abdomen

explanation: Dividing the abdomen into four quadrants helps pinpoint which internal organs might be causing the patient's pain. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T4#GNS111_U1_T4_h4)

question: What is the role of inhibin, a hormone released by Sertoli cells?

options.A: To signal the hypothalamus to stop all gonadotropin-releasing hormone production
options.B: To convert circulating testosterone into active dihydrotestosterone
options.C: To provide negative feedback that selectively decreases FSH release from the pituitary
options.D: To stimulate the immediate release of mature sperm into the epididymis

explanation: Think of inhibin as a messenger that tells the brain, 'We have enough sperm right now, you can slow down on releasing FSH!'

question: What is the most effective single measure to prevent the spread of infections in a hospital?

options.A: Changing bed linens twice daily
options.B: Wearing sterile gloves for every task
options.C: Performing proper hand hygiene
options.D: Spraying patient rooms with disinfectants

explanation: Hand hygiene remains the single most impactful action a nurse can take to break the chain of infection. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T3#GNS122_U2_T3_h2)

question: A patient calls the clinic panicking because their stool turned dark green after starting iron pills. What should you tell them?

options.A: Advise them to stop taking the iron tablets immediately and rush to the hospital
options.B: Reassure them that this is a harmless and expected side effect
options.C: Tell them to collect a stool sample to check for bleeding
options.D: Tell them to drink less water because it dilutes the drug

explanation: No need to panic! Unabsorbed iron naturally turns the stool dark green or black as it passes through. Giving this quick reassurance eases patient anxiety instantly.

question: What defines the oliguric stage of acute renal failure?

options.A: The complete absence of blood in the circulatory system
options.B: A sudden return of normal kidney filtering rates
options.C: A massive increase in daily urine production
options.D: A significant drop in daily urine output

explanation: During the oliguric stage, urine output decreases sharply, often dropping below 400 milliliters per day. [learn more](GNS213_U4_T6#GNS213_U4_T6_h3)

question: What dangerous event happens when severe swelling inside the skull pushes brain tissue downward?

options.A: Brain herniation
options.B: Ventriculomegaly
options.C: Cortical atrophy
options.D: Neural regeneration

explanation: Brain herniation is a medical emergency where high pressure forces brain tissue to shift where it shouldn't go. Keep up the good work!

question: How does uterine hyperstimulation lead to foetal hypoxia?

options.A: It shrinks the size of the umbilical cord vessels permanently
options.B: It prevents the placenta from refilling with oxygen between contractions
options.C: It forces the baby to breathe amniotic fluid too early
options.D: It causes the mother's blood pressure to rise dangerously high

explanation: If contractions are too close together without resting phases, blood flow through the uterine wall stops, starving the placenta of fresh oxygen. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T003#GNS226_U4_T003_h2)

question: Why do DRF programs love buying drugs by their generic names?

options.A: Patients refuse to take medications with brand names
options.B: Generic drugs do not require any regulatory inspection
options.C: Generic drugs are much cheaper than branded equivalents
options.D: Generic medications never expire on hospital pharmacy shelves

explanation: Generic drugs give us the same medical power as expensive brand names, but at a much lower cost—helping keep healthcare affordable for everyone.

question: On the AVPU neurological scale, what does the letter 'V' stand for?

options.A: Voice
options.B: Ventilation
options.C: Vomiting
options.D: Vascular

explanation: Remember AVPU: Alert, Voice-responsive, Pain-responsive, and Unresponsive. It's a quick and handy way to check mental status!

question: Which setting is best for an older adult who needs round-the-clock nursing checks and complex wound care?

options.A: Assisted living facility
options.B: Skilled nursing facility
options.C: Independent living apartment
options.D: Continuing care retirement community

explanation: Great thinking! A skilled nursing facility provides the 24/7 professional nursing oversight needed for heavy clinical tasks like complex wound care.

question: What is the very first thing you must do if you suspect your patient is having a transfusion reaction?

options.A: Administer emergency antihistamines
options.B: Collect a urine sample for testing
options.C: Stop the blood transfusion immediately
options.D: Notify the attending physician

explanation: Safety first! Stop the infusion right away to keep any more of that mismatched blood from entering their system. Every second counts.

question: What is the most common early sign of testicular cancer?

options.A: Sudden severe pain accompanied by a high fever
options.B: Recurrent urinary tract infections and visible blood
options.C: A painless, firm lump inside the testicle
options.D: Painful swelling of the entire scrotum during walking

explanation: Spot on! Early on, it usually just feels like a painless, hard lump. That is why monthly self-checks are a lifesaver.

question: What important advice should you give a patient who just got antibiotics for a bacterial STI?

options.A: Double the next dose if you forget to take one pill
options.B: Stop taking the pills the moment physical discomfort disappears
options.C: Complete the entire medication course even if symptoms resolve
options.D: Share remaining medication with your partner to save money

explanation: You got it! Even if they feel better in a few days, finishing all the pills ensures the bacteria are fully wiped out.

question: Staff nurses complain of severe exhaustion. Instead of just adding extra shifts, the manager investigates and discovers that broken equipment is causing major delays. What has the manager found?

options.A: A completely unrelated administrative task
options.B: The root cause of the exhaustion
options.C: An entirely programmed routine choice
options.D: The personal fault of the junior nurses

explanation: Brilliant! By looking past the surface complaints, the manager found the true source of the trouble.

question: What is the main reason a doctor would order an EEG test?

options.A: Locating tumors in the spinal column
options.B: Diagnosing and evaluating seizure disorders
options.C: Detecting blockages in carotid arteries
options.D: Measuring pressure inside the eye chambers

explanation: EEGs are most commonly used to catch those tricky abnormal electrical patterns linked with epilepsy and seizures. Super important clinical tool!

question: Why do care staff encourage residents to do parts of their morning routine all by themselves?

options.A: To reduce the total number of staff members needed on duty
options.B: To eliminate the need for any individualized service plans
options.C: To comply with federal acute care hospital regulations
options.D: To prevent physical decline caused by lack of use

explanation: Great thinking! Letting residents do what they can manage preserves their muscle strength, coordination, and sense of pride.

question: Why is communication especially critical for the home health care team compared to a hospital staff?

options.A: Hospital staff do not communicate with each other during shifts
options.B: Team members work independently in scattered locations rather than in one building
options.C: Home health personnel rarely document patient progress in charts
options.D: Patients manage their own medications without professional input
